checks_run: Inventoried all 51 submitted files, checked object types and permissions, and compared aggregate SHA-256 values before and after review.
Parsed MANIFEST.yaml and PROVENANCE.json as strict JSON and independently invoked the submitted structural/credential audit.
Ran the environment probe and recorded the available compiler, build tool, Python runtime, utilities, and unavailable analysis tools.
Built the starter and sealed reference from clean state with the submitted strict warning flags in a writable copy.
Ran all 15 public tests against the reference and both invocation tests against the starter.
Ran the sealed parser, job-table, integration, adversarial, and PTY suites under outer timeouts.
Reproduced the submitted ASan/UBSan link failure, then restored a normal clean reference build.
Reproduced both debugging-exercise outcomes, compiled the review exercise, and smoke-tested the benchmark driver with one iteration.
Built a parser-only milestone probe from the reference parser plus the unchanged starter executor and ran the invocation and parsing stages.
Ran reviewer-owned probes for exact whitespace grammar, mixed stopped/completed wait status, parse-before-launch, and a pipeline with initially closed standard input.
Reviewed progressive-disclosure layout, learner guidance, known-gap disclosures, license boundary, and provenance binding semantics.
evidence: The original CANDIDATE aggregate SHA-256 remained 8899c7982e7f1be65f82b60b840de076bf6dece10c6f97d42bf5cfa04da658d0; all candidate files remained immutable and no candidate file was edited.
Clean strict builds succeeded for starter/msh and sealed/reference/msh-reference with GCC 8.5.0.
Reference results reproduced: 15/15 public tests, 6 parser cases, 3 job-table cases, 11 integration tests, 4 adversarial tests, and 1 PTY test passed; starter invocation was 2/2.
Manifest claims are conservative: status is GENERATED, labels are GENERATED and PARTIAL, independent validation is REQUIRED, and productionized is false.

A mixed-state R4.4 probe created stopped job 1 and completed job 2 with status 7; msh_jobs_wait_all printed a stopped-job diagnostic and returned 1 instead of the specified highest-numbered completed-job status 7.
Vertical tab, form feed, and carriage return each split an unquoted argument into two, because parser.c uses isspace although R2.1 names only space, tab, and newline as separators.

The parser-only milestone binary passed 2/2 invocation tests but failed 3/3 parsing-stage tests solely because every parsing test executes an external command through the still-unimplemented starter executor.
With standard input initially closed, 'printf x | cat' returned 1 with empty stdout and an EBADF diagnostic; close_pipes closes fd 0 after dup2(0, 0).
The malformed command 'touch ... |' returned 2 and created no file, supporting the parse-before-launch invariant.
The documented sanitizer limitation reproduced exactly: linking could not find libasan.so.5.0.0 or libubsan.so.1.0.0 and exited 2.

The actual SHA-256 of PROVENANCE.json is 2ade2f5c7ca0f0af11d436e0fc18422ffe831635622addace3c9a75e3ca7f374, while MANIFEST.yaml provenance_sha256 is the separate snapshot identifier 8c9dfcfc0a7e11722572b7efd0dab0f02bca8ee03eb87027356598182ae4a9ee.
limitations: ASan/UBSan binaries could not be linked; valgrind, cppcheck, shellcheck, clang, rg, jq, and git were unavailable in this workspace.

The catalog source repository, linked tutorial, network, and immutable source snapshot were unavailable, so source-commit authenticity, catalog license evidence, and the no-copy/no-close-paraphrase assertion could not be independently verified.

No materialized learner view or transfer harness was supplied; exclusion of sealed/reference, sealed tests, canonical answers, and evaluator-facing adversarial material from the actual student view remains inconclusive.

No cross-platform, randomized fuzzing, coverage, deterministic allocation/syscall failure injection, low-resource-limit, PID-reuse, extended PTY, leak, or production-readiness validation was performed.
Candidate-authored test success was treated only as supporting evidence and does not award BUILDS, TESTED, FUZZED, BENCHMARKED, REVIEWED, TRANSFER_VERIFIED, or PRODUCTIONIZED.
